properties.decision:
RECORDED AS A FINDING, 2026-08-19, split out of `fact:changing-one-sentence-in-a-long-decision-cost-a-full-6242-character-resend` because it had been filed under the wrong fix. Nothing built, nothing asked for.

**WHAT HAPPENED, twice in one session.** A `Decision` was written with a closing tag and the `rationale` ARGUMENT emitted inside the `decision` parameter. Both calls **succeeded**. What landed was a decision body ending in tool-call markup, and no `rationale` property at all:

  1. `dec:idea-parks-shipped-...` — body ended `</decision>` then `<parameter name="rationale">…`
  2. `dec:idea-what-is-reflow2s-part-in-an-automated-translation` — body ended `</decision>` then `<rationale>…</rationale></invoke>`

**NO LAYER NOTICED.** Not the schema (a string is a string), not `undeclared` (the property is declared and was simply absent), not the revision block (it faithfully reported replacing one property — it just cannot know the replacement is corrupt), not the dedup guard, not `detect_defects`. Both were caught only because the reply was read. **A design brain silently carrying `</invoke>` inside a Decision's prose is a worse outcome than any awkward edit**, because everything downstream — `search_design`'s index, the embedding field, a `where-am-i` narration, an export a person reads — treats it as content.

🛑 **AND IT IS NOT THE `resolve_decision` CASE.** Both were FIRST writes of NEW nodes. A resolution-append tool would not have been reachable and would have prevented neither. Filing these with the resend measurement was an error, corrected the same day when Anthony asked for the evidence to be walked through.

✅ **MEASURED, AND IT IS THE REASSURING ANSWER: THIS IS NEW, NOT LONG-STANDING.** The committed export was scanned — all 2,607 nodes, every string property, for closing tool-call tags and `<parameter name=` — and found **0**. So no earlier session left absorbed markup in this graph, and the two instances above (both since corrected) are the only ones. The scan is ~10 lines of Python and is the cheap form of the check any guard would institutionalise.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, and none is as cheap as it first looks

**A. Reject a text property whose value contains tool-call markup.**
   ⚠️ COUNTER, AND IT IS FATAL TO THE NAIVE FORM: this very node, and the fact it was split from, both quote `</decision>` and `</invoke>` ON PURPOSE — and the scan above found exactly those two as its only hits once they existed. A rule matching those strings anywhere would refuse the only two nodes in the design that document the bug. Any guard has to key on SHAPE — markup at the TAIL of a value, immediately followed by what parses as another parameter name — not on the strings appearing at all.

**B. Warn rather than refuse.** Surface it the way `undeclared` surfaces an unknown property: the write lands, the reply says "this value ends in what looks like a tool-call boundary". Cheaper, no false-refusal risk, and it fails in the safe direction. ⚠️ But it inherits `undeclared`'s own disease if it ever fires on correct writes — which is the exact complaint hxm_program filed about `ChangeEvent.description`.

**C. A periodic scan rather than a write-time check.** The 10-line scan above, run in CI over the committed export. Catches the class with no false-refusal risk and no per-write cost, at the price of finding it later rather than at the moment of the write. ⚠️ Later may be fine here: the failure is silent but not destructive — nothing else breaks while it sits.

**D. Do nothing, and treat it as a caller defect.** Defensible: the caller emitted a malformed call and the transport accepted it. ⚠️ Counter: reflow2's whole posture is that a silent wrong write is worse than a loud refusal, and this is a silent wrong write. `dec:two-sided-accept` and the dedup guard both exist because the design does not trust a write to be right just because it parsed.

**E. The generalisation worth naming.** `cap:a-revising-write-says-whether-the-state-survived` computes whether the REPLACED state survived. Nothing computes whether the REPLACEMENT is plausible. Those are different questions and only the first is built.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️ HONEST BOUNDS, stated so this is not over-read

· n = 2, one session, one caller, one model. Not a rate.
· Both were on parameters over 4,000 characters, and none of roughly thirty short writes the same day malformed — suggestive that long free-text arguments are where boundaries get mis-emitted, but observational and confounded, since the long writes also carry the most retyped text.
· NO USER REPORTED THIS. It is a self-host observation, and by `dec:idea-field-evidence-is-a-prioritisation-input` it ranks below anything two projects filed this week. What makes it worth recording at all is that the failure is SILENT and lands in the durable record.
· STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any USER's graph carries such markup. Only this design was scanned, and it is the one graph whose caller is known.
properties.name: OPEN — a prose field swallowed tool-call markup and the write SUCCEEDED: nothing refuses, flags or notices a node whose body ends in `</decision><rationale>…</invoke>`
properties.rationale:
Split into its own node rather than left inside the resend fact because the two were filed together only by coincidence of timing, and that coincidence led to a wrong recommendation — that `resolve_decision` would fix both. It fixes one. Recorded as an open question rather than a proposal because the obvious guard is not obvious: the naive string match would refuse the very nodes that document the defect, which is a good reason to think before building. Kept explicitly below the field-reported items in priority, per the design's own rule that field evidence outranks self-host observation, so that recording it does not smuggle it up the queue. The dedup guard named the fact it was split from, which is correct behaviour and was read before declaring them distinct — the split is deliberate, not an accident of wording.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ ACCEPTED 2026-08-31, ANTHONY'S WORD. THE CHOSEN SHAPE IS A's KEYING WITH B's SEVERITY.

WHAT IS BUILT: a WARNING, never a refusal, that fires when a prose field names a parameter via `<parameter name="X">` where **X is a declared parameter of the tool being called AND X was not supplied in that call**. It detects the LOSS rather than the syntax.

⭐ THIS NODE ALREADY SPECIFIED IT. Option A's counter-argument reads: "Any guard has to key on SHAPE — markup at the TAIL of a value, immediately followed by what parses as another parameter name — not on the strings appearing at all." That is the accepted design, arrived at independently on 2026-08-31 and then found already written here. Option B supplied the severity: warn, do not refuse, failing in the safe direction.

📐 THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT WAS TESTED AGAINST THE REAL GRAPH BEFORE ANY CODE, and it is quantified rather than assumed:
    naive "contains the markup at all"            3 false positives — all three are nodes ABOUT this defect, including THIS one
    "names a parameter the node lacks"            2 false positives — both TemporalFacts, a type with no `rationale` parameter
    type-scoped to the tool's OWN declared params 0 false positives across 1,776 nodes
The middle row is why the check is scoped to the typed `add_*` tools rather than applied to every string in the store: `create_node` takes a `props` bag with no declared prose parameters, so the question "was the named parameter supplied?" has no meaning there.

🛑 AND THE BOUND THIS NODE FLAGGED AS UNRESOLVED IS NOW RESOLVED, WHICH IS WHAT MOVED IT. It closed with "NO USER REPORTED THIS. It is a self-host observation... STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any USER's graph carries such markup." A consumer project hit it twice on 2026-08-31 — `proj:bhome`, a pod dwelling with no connection to reflow2's subject matter, on `add_decision` and `add_change_event` — and independently proposed the same warn-don't-reject fix. See `fact:bhome-confirms-two-known-causes-and-supplies-the-measurements-both-were-waiting-on`. Seven instances now across two projects and two graphs; the self-host caveat no longer applies.

📌 bhome ALSO ADDED A CONSEQUENCE THIS NODE DOES NOT RECORD: the bleed swallows subsequent STRUCTURED parameters, not only prose. One node landed with the markup in `decision`, no `rationale`, AND none of three `related_to` relations — so `unreviewed_ideas` could not fire either, because the node genuinely had none. That strengthens the case for warning at the write: three separate silences, one cause.

⚠️ WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: option C's periodic CI scan. The write-time warning reaches the moment the author can still fix it cheaply; a scan finds it later and the two are not equivalent. C stays available and is not foreclosed. Option D (do nothing) is declined on the ground this node itself argues — reflow2's posture is that a silent wrong write is worse than a loud refusal, and this is a silent wrong write.
